instrument: Grenada Citizenship by Investment (Amendment) Bill, 2026 — clause 8, inserting new s. 7A into the Grenada Citizenship by Investment Act No. 15 of 2013
articles: clause 1(2) (short title and commencement); clause 8, new s. 7A(2)(a), 7A(4), 7A(11), 7A(12); clause 8, new s. 7B(6)
quote_original: at least thirty (30) days during or up to any of the first five (5)
data_change_needed: No change to grenada-cbi presence fields. Keep the PENDING note. Separate, newly verified fact worth recording in the note: Grenada's Eastern Caribbean Citizenship by Investment Regulatory Authority Agreement Act, 2025 (Act No 19 of 2025) was brought into force by S.R.&O. No. 12 of 2026, notified in Government Gazette Vol. 144 No. 34 of 24 July 2026 — i.e. the DOMESTICATING act has commenced even though the 30-day rule in the CBI Act has not.
notes: NOT YET IN FORCE. The bill is real and the lead's 30-day characterisation is accurate; the mechanism in the lead ('~30 days presence within five years') understates it, because there are two limbs: an aggregate of 30 days across the main applicant AND dependants over the first five calendar years (s. 7A(2)(a), (3), (5)), plus an individual floor of five days each in the first twelve months (s. 7A(4), verbatim: 'dependant named in the application resulting in the grant of citizenship'). Commencement is open-ended — clause 1(2) verbatim: 'This Act shall come into force on a date to be appointed by the Minister' (continuing 'by Order published in the Gazette.'). No such Order for the CBI (Amendment) Act exists as at 21 August 2026. Negative evidence, both from official sources: (1) laws.gov.gd's 2026 Acts folder (https://laws.gov.gd/index.php/acts/1376-2026) lists only Acts No. 1-5 of 2026 (Drug Abuse (Prevention and Control) (Amendment); Trademarks (Amendment); Banking (Amendment); CARICOM Arrest Warrant; Domestic Violence (Amendment)) — no CBI amendment; (2) I fetched and text-searched every Grenada Government Gazette published from 17 July to 14 August 2026 (Nos. 33, 34, 35, 36, 37 extraordinary, and 38 of 2026) and the ONLY citizenship item in any of them is the S.R.&O. No. 12 of 2026 notice in No. 34, which commences the ECCIRA Agreement Act, not this bill. Further conditionality even after commencement: new s. 7B(6) provides that ss. 7A and 7B 'apply to applications submitted on or after the coming into force of the ECCIRA Agreement Act and may be applied retroactively to pending applications at the discretion of the Minister, subject to transitional guidelines.' Also in the bill: passports issued to CBI citizens carry an initial five-year validity renewable to ten only on certification of compliance (s. 7A(11)); failure without reasonable excuse is a ground to initiate revocation (s. 7A(12)); exemption on humanitarian/compassionate grounds (s. 7A(9)). Clause 8's text is a near-verbatim domestication of ECCIRA Agreement Article 48 — see the ATG row for the Agreement text.

instrument: The Eastern Caribbean Citizenship by Investment Regulatory Authority Agreement Act 2025, No. 18 of 2025 (Antigua and Barbuda), incorporating the ECCIRA Agreement as a Schedule
articles: s. 1(2) (commencement); s. 4(1)-(2) (Agreement to have force of law); Schedule, Agreement Articles 48.2(a), 48.4, 48.11, 48.12, 95.1, 96.1-96.2
quote_original: (2) This Act shall come into force on a date to be appointed by the Minister by Order
data_change_needed: No change to antigua-barbuda-cip presence fields (leave at 5 days). Keep the PENDING note but CORRECT its instrument: the note should cite the Eastern Caribbean Citizenship by Investment Regulatory Authority Agreement Act 2025, No. 18 of 2025 (gazetted 6 November 2025, awaiting a Ministerial commencement Order), not a 'CIP Amendment Bill 2026'.
notes: NOT YET IN FORCE. The lead's premise is wrong in its instrument. There is no 'Antigua and Barbuda Citizenship by Investment (Amendment) Bill 2026'. I checked the official bills index (https://laws.gov.ag/bills/, 51 bill PDFs, 2025-2026, no CIP amendment) and separately searched the whole of laws.gov.ag via its WordPress media API for 'Citizenship' (27 hits; the newest CIP-family instruments are No. 50 of 2024 CBI (Amendment) Regulations and No. 25 of 2020 CBI (Amendment) Act). What DOES exist, and is the real vehicle for 5 days -> 30 days, is Act No. 18 of 2025, whose cover page reads '[Published in the Official Gazette Vol. XLV No. 60' (dated 6th November, 2025). It is assented and gazetted, so it is ENACTED, but s. 1(2) leaves commencement to a Ministerial Order published in the Gazette and I found no such Order. Its Schedule is the ECCIRA Agreement, and s. 4(1) gives the Agreement 'the force of law in Antigua and Barbuda'; s. 4(2) then says 'The Agreement shall enter into force in accordance with Article 95.' TWO independent conditions therefore gate the 30 days in Antigua: the Ministerial commencement Order, AND the Agreement's own entry into force. Article 95.1 verbatim: 'This Agreement shall enter into force on the thirtieth (30th) day following the date of' (continuing 'deposit of the fifth (5th) instrument of ratification.'). Article 96 allows provisional application once three Participating States declare an intention to apply it provisionally. Article 48.2(a) verbatim (this is the operative 30-day obligation, and it is identical across the region): 'aggregate of at least thirty (30) days during or up to any of the first five (5)'. Article 48.4 adds the individual five-day floor in the first twelve months. I did NOT find the instrument that sources the atlas's existing 5-day figure — it is not in Act No. 10 of 2018 (which concerns the Board); it is presumably in the CBI Regulations and was not re-verified in this pass.

instrument: Законопроект за изменение и допълнение на Закона за чужденците в Република България, вх. № 52-602-01-29 (Bill to amend and supplement the Law on Foreigners in the Republic of Bulgaria), 52nd National Assembly, submitted 28 July 2026 by the Council of Ministers under Decision No. 575 of 27 July 2026
articles: § 17, item 2, creating art. 40(1)(24) of the Law on Foreigners in the Republic of Bulgaria (Закон за чужденците в Република България); cf. § 17 item 1 amending art. 40(1)(6); § 11 amending art. 25(1) items 6, 7, 8, 16
quote_original: не е пребивавал на територията на Република България през предходната календарна година най-малко 6 месеца и
quote_translation: has not resided on the territory of the Republic of Bulgaria during the preceding calendar year for at least 6 months and [one day]
data_change_needed: TWO changes. (1) DEFECT FIX, authorable now, independent of the bill: set physical_presence_days_per_year from 0 to null. The 0 is an unexamined default, not a sourced figure — see notes for the proof. (2) Add the PENDING note that was missed when the row was marked checked on 2026-08-20: a government bill would create a ground to WITHDRAW permanent residence where the holder did not reside in Bulgaria for at least 6 months and one day in the preceding calendar year; introduced 28 July 2026, not enacted, not published in Държавен вестник as at 21 August 2026.
notes: NOT YET IN FORCE. Bill verified via the National Assembly's own JSON API at https://www.parliament.bg/api/v1/bill/167465 — the HTML page at /bg/bills/ID/167465 is a 4,304-byte Vue router shell and returns the identical body for any path, so it proves nothing. The API record confirms: L_Act_sign '52-602-01-29', L_Act_date '2026-07-28', session 'Първа сесия', withdrawn false, lead committee Комисия по вътрешна сигурност и обществен ред, distributed to committees by order 52-650-01-236 of 2026-07-30. NOT ENACTED: L_Act_dv_ID is -1, L_Act_dv_iss and L_ActL_final are empty strings and L_Act_dv_year is null (no Държавен вестник publication), and stan_list, stan_list2, steno_hall and activity are all empty (no plenary reading recorded). The bill contains no 'влиза в сила' clause, so on enactment the constitutional default would apply (three days after promulgation in Държавен вестник); effective_date is therefore genuinely unknown, not merely unstated. TWO SUBSTANTIVE CORRECTIONS TO THE LEAD'S FRAMING. First, this is not an eligibility presence requirement — art. 40 ZChRB is the withdrawal-of-residence article, so the new item 24 is a REVOCATION ground for an existing permanent residence permit. Second, and load-bearing for the golden-visa route: the new item 24 carries NO carve-out for investor permanent residence, whereas § 17 item 1's rewrite of art. 40(1)(6) (long-term residence) expressly preserves 'разрешено постоянно пребиваване по чл. 25, ал. 1, т. 6-8, 13 и 16 и чл. 25г' — the investment grounds. On the face of the text the investor PR holder is inside item 24 and outside item 6's protection. WHY THE 0 IS UNSOURCED: § 17 item 2 opens 'Създават се т. 24 и 25' ('items 24 and 25 are created'). A ground that is being created does not presently exist, so no instrument states a presence figure for Bulgarian permanent residence — neither zero nor any other number. The bill's own motives confirm the gap in policy terms: 'увеличеният брой заявления на чужденци с цел пребиваване на територията на страната води до необходимост от създаване на условия за по-стриктен контрол върху пребиваването на чужденци с разрешено право на постоянно пребиваване в Република България'. That is a statement that stricter control must be CREATED, not a statement that zero days are required. Per the house rule (null means NOT RECORDED, never 'not required' and never zero), the field should be null. If the bill is later enacted, record the requirement as stated — 'най-малко 6 месеца и един ден' per preceding calendar year, i.e. in months, not as a derived day count; I have deliberately left presence_days_required null rather than write 183, which appears in no instrument. Unrelated but adjacent: § 11 redenominates the art. 25(1) investment thresholds from leva to euro (art. 25(1)(6)(a) 2,000,000 лв. -> 1,022,583.76 евро; (6)(b) and (6)(c)/(6)(d) base 1,000,000 лв. -> 511,291.88 евро; (7) 2,000,000 лв. -> 1,022,583.76 евро; (8) 6,000,000 лв. -> 3,067,751.29 евро; (16) 500,000 лв. -> 255,645.94 евро) — worth a look against whatever amount the row currently carries, since Bulgaria adopted the euro on 1 January 2026. NOTE ON SOURCING: imidaily.com was not used as authority; the discovery URL on #228 led only to the parliament ID, and everything above comes from parliament.bg.

instrument: Citizenship by Investment (Amendment) Act, No. 22 of 2025 (Saint Lucia), s. 8, inserting new s. 30A into the Citizenship by Investment Act, Cap. 1.20
articles: s. 8, new s. 30A(1) and 30A(2); Act commencement date [10th November, 2025]; assent 3 November 2025; cf. s. 3 (new definitions 'OECS Member State', 'Treaty of Basseterre'), s. 9(d) (new s. 36(3)(b))
quote_original: shall comply with the prescribed requirements for
data_change_needed: THIS IS THE COVERAGE GAP AND IT IS AUTHORABLE NOW. saint-lucia-cip carries no PENDING note and was last checked 2026-07-30, but Saint Lucia already has an IN-FORCE post-grant residency and genuine-link obligation: s. 30A of the CBI Act, inserted by Act No. 22 of 2025 (commenced 10 November 2025), with s. 30A(1) taking effect from 1 January 2026. Record the obligation and its effective date. Do NOT record a day count — presence_days_required must be null, because the Act delegates the content to 'the prescribed requirements' and no regulation has prescribed them.
notes: IN FORCE, BUT EMPTY OF CONTENT. Saint Lucia is the answer to question 2 that the leads missed: it is neither 'proposed' nor 'genuinely absent' — it is enacted and commenced, ahead of both Grenada and Antigua. Act No. 22 of 2025 was assented by Governor-General Errol Charles on November 3, 2025 and bears the commencement date '[ 10th November, 2025 ]'. Section 8 inserts s. 30A, headed 'Residency and genuine link requirments' (the misspelling is in the enacted text): '30A.—(1) Where an application for citizenship by investment is made under section 30, an applicant and each qualifying dependant shall comply with the prescribed requirements for residency and genuine link. (2) Subsection (1) takes effect from the 1st day of January, 2026.' Verbatim single-line fragment for the date limb, if a second quote is wanted: 'takes effect from the 1st day of January,'. THE DAY COUNT DOES NOT EXIST IN SAINT LUCIAN LAW YET. 'Prescribed' means prescribed by regulations, and the requirements have not been prescribed: I fetched the most recent instrument, Citizenship by Investment (Amendment) Regulations, S.I. No. 57 of 2026, gazetted 23 March 2026 (Vol. 195, Issue 6, Extraordinary Gazette of Monday March 23, 2026, made 20 March 2026), and it does not touch residency or genuine link — it amends regulations 2, 7 and 9 on other matters, and its only 'thirty days' is a proof-filing window ('period not exceeding thirty days to provide the required proof'). I also enumerated the CIU's full official legislation list (19 instruments, 2015-2026, at https://www.cipsaintlucia.com/citizenship-legislation) and no instrument on it prescribes a presence figure. So the correct atlas state is: obligation recorded, effective 2026-01-01, days null (NOT RECORDED — not zero, and not 30 by inference from ECCIRA). ECCIRA LINK IS UNPROVEN, hence eccira_linked null: Saint Lucia signed the ECCIRA Agreement on 22 September 2025 (per the Agreement's own signature block, see the ATG row source), and Act No. 22 of 2025 imports OECS machinery (s. 3 defines 'OECS Member State' by reference to the Treaty of Basseterre, and new s. 36(3)(b) lets the Board deny an application denied by an OECS Member State) — but the Act nowhere names ECCIRA or Article 48, and s. 30A's 1 January 2026 date is not tied to the Agreement's entry into force. Saint Lucia appears to have legislated the hook domestically and independently of the Agreement's commencement machinery, which is materially different from the Antigua and Grenada designs.

instrument: Eastern Caribbean Citizenship by Investment Regulatory Authority (ECCIRA) Bill, 2025 — reported passed by the National Assembly on 17 October 2025; enacted Act text and any commencement order not located
articles: would domesticate ECCIRA Agreement Article 48 (30-day aggregate presence, five-day individual floor in first twelve months)
data_change_needed: Nothing authorable. Do not add a presence row or figure. If a note is wanted, it must say only what is verified: Saint Kitts and Nevis signed the ECCIRA Agreement on 18 September 2025, and its Citizenship by Investment Unit states the ECCIRA Bill 2025 was passed on 17 October 2025; the Act text and any commencement order could not be located.
notes: CANNOT DETERMINE, and I am naming the blocker rather than substituting a press release for an instrument. VERIFIED: Saint Kitts and Nevis is one of the five Participating States in the ECCIRA Agreement Annex, and Prime Minister Dr. Terrence M. Drew signed the Agreement on 18 September 2025 — that is quotable from the Agreement's signature block (see the ATG row source_url), not from Saint Kitts sources. REPORTED ONLY: the Citizenship by Investment Unit's own site carries a post titled 'ST. KITTS AND NEVIS PASSES ECCIRA BILL 2025', dated November 14, 2025, stating the ECCIRA Bill 2025 was passed on October 17, 2025 and that ECCIRA 'will now have the legal mandate'. That is an official-domain press release, not a gazette or an Act, it gives no commencement date, and it does not mention a 30-day presence requirement at all — so under the house rule it establishes nothing recordable. WHAT I TRIED AND WHY IT FAILED: https://ciu.gov.kn/legislation/ returns 404 (the site serves a 134KB themed 404, so a status check alone would have been misleading); ciu.gov.kn's WordPress sitemap index exposes only post, page, category, post_tag and author sitemaps, no document or legislation post type; the only PDF anywhere on ciu.gov.kn is ChairmanUpdate_December2025__F.pdf; and on the main government site www.gov.kn the paths /gazettes/, /documents/ and /legislation/ all 404 (each returning a ~265KB themed 404 page). I could not locate a Saint Kitts and Nevis gazette archive or statute repository at all, so I can neither confirm nor exclude an enacted ECCIRA Agreement Act or a commencement order. NEXT STEP for whoever picks this up: the Saint Christopher and Nevis Official Gazette is not on gov.kn; try the Attorney General's Chambers / Ministry of Legal Affairs, or request the Act number directly from the CIU.

instrument: Commonwealth of Dominica Citizenship by Investment (Amendment) Regulations, 2025, S.R.O. No. 46 of 2025 (most recent published CBI instrument); no ECCIRA domesticating Act located
articles: S.R.O. No. 46 of 2025, regs. 1-3 (amendment of Schedule 1, para. 3(1) of the Commonwealth of Dominica Citizenship by Investment Regulations 2024, S.R.O. No. 8 of 2024), made under s. 20 of the Commonwealth of Dominica Citizenship Act, Chapter 1:10
data_change_needed: Nothing authorable, and in particular DO NOT add an absence row or an absence footnote — silence is how the atlas says a thing does not exist. If a research note is wanted: no post-grant physical-presence requirement appears in any CBI instrument published by Dominica's Citizenship by Investment Unit, and Dominica's domestication of the ECCIRA Agreement it signed on 18 September 2025 could not be confirmed either way.
notes: CANNOT DETERMINE, with a specific and stated blocker. VERIFIED: Dominica is a Participating State in the ECCIRA Agreement Annex and Prime Minister Roosevelt Skerrit signed the Agreement on 18 September 2025 (quotable from the Agreement signature block — see the ATG row source_url). NEGATIVE EVIDENCE, official: I enumerated the complete legislation list published by Dominica's own Citizenship by Investment Unit at the source_url. It holds four items — the Commonwealth of Dominica Citizenship Act, S.R.O. No. 8 of 2024 (CBI (Amendment) (No. 2) Regulations 2024), the Constitution, and CBI-Amendment-Regulation-2025.pdf. There is no ECCIRA Agreement Act, no ECCIRA bill, and no instrument whose title suggests residency, presence or genuine link. WHAT THE 2025 INSTRUMENT ACTUALLY DOES, and why it is not quote-gated: CBI-Amendment-Regulation-2025.pdf is Commonwealth of Dominica S.R.O. 46, Statutory Rules and Orders No. 46 of 2025, made by the Minister under s. 20 of the Commonwealth of Dominica Citizenship Act, Chapter 1:10, gazetted 27th November 2025, made 26th November 2025, signed Daren Pinard, Minister for Citizenship, cited as the Commonwealth of Dominica Citizenship by Investment (Amendment) Regulations, 2025. Its single operative provision amends Schedule 1 to the 2024 Principal Regulations in paragraph 3(1) by deleting the words 'not more than five years after the main applicant obtained citizenship'. That is a timing window for an application step, NOT a presence requirement — it moves in the opposite direction from ECCIRA Article 48 by removing a five-year limit rather than adding one. I read that content visually from a rendered page image, NOT from a text layer: the PDF is a 1-page 14,915-byte scan produced by a Xerox WorkCentre 6515DN, a single JBIG2Decode image with no extractable text, so pdftotext returns zero bytes. I have therefore left quote_original null on purpose — any quote I wrote from it would fail research:verify:quotes on re-fetch, because there is no text at the URL to match. The same blocker applies to the Commonwealth of Dominica Citizenship Act PDF on the CBIU site (1,038,811 bytes, also no text layer), which is where an existing presence requirement would live if one existed. So: no equivalent presence requirement is published, but I cannot prove absence from the primary Act, and I cannot confirm or exclude an ECCIRA domesticating Act. NEXT STEP: the Dominica Official Gazette is not served from dominica.gov.dm (/gazettes 404s, /laws returns a 31-byte stub); an OCR pass over the two scanned PDFs, or the Government Printery in Roseau, would close this.
